findings.title: Registered metric-alert handler is now uninstantiable
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates that class with no try/except. Any detector whose type slug is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError inside process_detectors and abort the whole batch. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty result, so the same detector was a no-op instead of a crash.

findings.title: Group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...), so its fingerprint is derived from group key "val1". The call under test is evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", 10, ...), and StatefulDetectorHandler passes that group key into build_occurrence_and_event_data, which fingerprints "group_key". IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so this assertion cannot pass. The value passed to the helper (6) also does not match the evaluated value (10).

findings.title: Occurrence test helper ignores the evaluated value, so the new hook is not actually checked
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never uses it, and MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data just calls that helper. Every new assertion rebuilds the expected occurrence with the same helper, so a regression that drops or swaps the value argument still passes. The inputs already disagree with the expectations: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate uses packet values 100 and 8 while expecting occurrences built with 6. Those tests therefore do not lock in the contract this PR adds.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on .values() of that dict. The docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, which will mislead callers that were updated for the signature change.
